title: Design a ride-sharing service
prompt: Riders open the app and need a nearby driver in seconds while millions of drivers stream GPS pings every few seconds. The dominant forcing constraint is GEO read-skew: matching must answer "who is near me?" against constantly-moving hot location data far faster than a database can serve. Draw how a ride request flows from a rider through an entry tier into a matching/location service, how hot driver-location and geo lookups are served from a cache, where trips and users are durably stored, and how trip events and notifications fan out asynchronously. Several valid topologies should pass — show the forcing components and how they connect.

criteria.label: Rider/driver client originates the request
criteria.metWhy: Good — the flow starts from the rider/driver client.
criteria.why: Add a User/Client node to represent the rider and driver apps that initiate requests and stream location.

criteria.label: Entry tier fronts the service (load balancer or API gateway)
criteria.metWhy: Good — an entry tier spreads traffic across the matching fleet.
criteria.why: Add a Load Balancer or API Gateway in front of your service so high-frequency location pings and ride requests are distributed.

criteria.label: A matching/location service handles requests
criteria.metWhy: Good — a compute tier performs matching and location processing.
criteria.why: Add a Server (or API Gateway acting as the service) to run the rider-driver matching and location logic.

criteria.label: Hot driver-location / geo lookups served from a cache
criteria.metWhy: Cache absorbs the geo read-skew — nearby-driver lookups stay fast under constant GPS updates.
criteria.why: The 'who is near me?' query repeats constantly against moving data — add a Cache (e.g. geo/Redis) for hot driver-location lookups.

criteria.label: Trips and users persisted in a durable datastore
criteria.metWhy: Durable source of truth for trips, users, and ride history.
criteria.why: Add a Database to durably store trips, users, and ride records — the cache alone is not durable.

criteria.label: Trip events / notifications handled asynchronously via a queue
criteria.metWhy: Queue decouples trip events and notification fan-out from the request path.
criteria.why: Trip state changes and driver/rider notifications should not block matching — add a Queue for async trip events and fan-out.

criteria.label: Service reads geo data through the cache
criteria.metWhy: The matching service queries the geo cache for nearby drivers.
criteria.why: Connect your matching Service to the Cache so nearby-driver lookups hit the fast path.

criteria.label: Service persists trips to the database
criteria.metWhy: The service writes trips/users to the durable store.
criteria.why: Connect your matching Service to the Database so trips and user records are persisted.

criteria.label: Service publishes trip events to the queue
criteria.metWhy: Trip events flow into the queue for async processing and notifications.
criteria.why: Connect your matching Service to the Queue so trip events and notifications are dispatched asynchronously.
